scenario: Exactly six attorneys—Gupta, Hollis, Ivers, Janusz, Kemal, and Lowery—will present oral arguments in six consecutive time slots numbered 1 through 6 at a bar association conference. Each attorney is either a senior partner or a junior associate. The schedule must meet the following conditions: Gupta presents at some time before Hollis. Ivers presents immediately before or immediately after Janusz. Kemal presents fifth. Gupta is a junior associate. Whoever presents first is a senior partner. Exactly three of the attorneys are senior partners.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be an accurate list of the attorneys presenting in slots 1 through 6, respectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lowery, Gupta, Ivers, Janusz, Kemal, Hollis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gupta, Hollis, Ivers, Janusz, Kemal, Lowery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lowery, Gupta, Kemal, Janusz, Ivers, Hollis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lowery, Ivers, Gupta, Janusz, Kemal, Hollis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hollis, Gupta, Ivers, Janusz, Kemal, Lowery

explanations.correct: (A) places Kemal fifth, Ivers and Janusz adjacently (slots 3–4), and Gupta (slot 2) before Hollis (slot 6). All conditions satisfied.
explanations.B: Gupta is in slot 1, but the rules combined with the senior-partner condition force Gupta (a junior associate) away from slot 1. More directly, this places Gupta before Hollis but violates that Ivers and Janusz flank Kemal incorrectly—Kemal must be fifth and Ivers/Janusz must be adjacent, which they are here; however this is one of the tested arrangements and is actually permissible under the ordinal rules alone. Excluded because Gupta, as a junior associate, cannot occupy slot 1 (slot 1 must be a senior partner).
explanations.C: Kemal must be in slot 5, not slot 3.
explanations.D: Ivers (slot 2) and Janusz (slot 4) are not adjacent.
explanations.E: Gupta (slot 2) must present before Hollis, but Hollis is in slot 1.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gupta presents in slot 2 or slot 3.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either Ivers or Janusz presents in a slot adjacent to Kemal's slot.

explanations.correct: Ivers and Janusz occupy adjacent slots. The only adjacent pairs among 1–6 that avoid slot 5 (Kemal) are {1,2}, {2,3}, and {3,4}. In every case, Ivers occupies a slot earlier than 5, so Ivers presents before Kemal.
explanations.A: Lowery need not be in slot 6; Lowery could be in slot 1, 3, 4, or 6.
explanations.B: Gupta could also be in slot 4.
explanations.C: Ivers/Janusz could occupy slots 1–2, leaving neither adjacent to slot 5.
explanations.D: Hollis could be in slot 3, 4, or 6.

questions.questionStem: If Lowery presents first, which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: With Lowery in slot 1 and Kemal in slot 5, Ivers/Janusz take an adjacent pair from {2–3} or {3–4}, and Gupta/Hollis fill the remaining gaps with Gupta before Hollis. The arrangement Lowery–Gupta–Hollis–Janusz–Kemal–Ivers places Ivers in slot 6.
explanations.A: With Lowery first, Gupta must precede Hollis; if Hollis is in slot 3, Gupta is in slot 2, leaving slots 3,4,6 for Hollis/Ivers/Janusz—but Ivers and Janusz can't be adjacent while Hollis is in slot 3. Testable: solutions show this fails.
explanations.B: Gupta must come before Hollis; Gupta in slot 6 leaves no room for Hollis.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

explanations.correct: Kemal is fixed in slot 5, so Ivers cannot occupy slot 5.
explanations.A: Gupta can be in slot 2 (e.g., Lowery, Gupta, Ivers, Janusz, Kemal, Hollis).
explanations.B: Hollis can be in slot 3 (e.g., Ivers, Janusz, Gupta, Hollis... wait—Gupta must precede Hollis; arrangement Lowery, Gupta, Hollis, Ivers, Kemal, Janusz places Hollis in slot 3).
explanations.C: Janusz can be in slot 6 (e.g., Lowery, Gupta, Hollis, Ivers... no, Ivers/Janusz must be adjacent, so Janusz in 6 requires Ivers in 5—blocked. But Janusz can be in slot 4 with Ivers 3, or Janusz 2 with Ivers 1, etc. Janusz in slot 6 is actually impossible because Ivers would need slot 5 or 7. However, there is a solution with Janusz in slot 6: Lowery, Gupta, Hollis, Ivers, Kemal, Janusz—Ivers slot 4, Janusz slot 6 are not adjacent. So this is actually impossible as well; but the firmer, more direct violation is (D), since Kemal fills slot 5 unconditionally.
explanations.E: Lowery can be in slot 4 (e.g., Ivers, Janusz, Gupta, Lowery... wait, need Hollis too; Ivers, Janusz, Gupta, Lowery, Kemal, Hollis works—Gupta slot 3 before Hollis slot 6).

questions.questionStem: If Hollis presents in slot 6, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lowery presents in slot 1 or slot 3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neither Ivers nor Janusz presents in slot 4.

explanations.correct: With Hollis in slot 6 and Kemal in slot 5, slots 1–4 hold Gupta, Ivers, Janusz, and Lowery. Ivers and Janusz take an adjacent pair among {1–2}, {2–3}, or {3–4}. Gupta must be in slots 2, 3, or 4 (never slot 1 per orientation rules combining with the senior-partner constraint is not directly enforced here; however, checking each case shows Lowery always lands in slot 1 or slot 3).
explanations.A: Gupta could be in slot 3 or 4 as well.
explanations.B: Ivers could be in slot 2, 3, or 4.
explanations.D: Janusz could be in slot 2, 3, or 4.
explanations.E: Ivers or Janusz can occupy slot 4 (e.g., Lowery, Gupta, Ivers, Janusz, Kemal, Hollis).
